summary: Tested brute-force login protection (backend pytest, 9 tests) and logout redirect + role regression (Playwright). Brute-force protection works end-to-end (401 x4 -> 429 lockout -> 429 countdown, per-email counters, counter cleared on success, toast shown in UI). LOGOUT REDIRECT IS BROKEN: both admin and worker land on generic /login instead of /beauty-studio-bor/admin/login. Root cause: ProtectedRoute in App.js renders <Navigate to="/login" replace/> the moment user becomes null after logout(), which wins over the navigate() call in AdminDashboard.handleLogout. Auth hygiene verified: bcrypt $2b$12$ hashes, httpOnly access/refresh cookies on login, app-level CORS returns explicit origin + allow-credentials true.

minor.issue: Spec says first 3 wrong attempts show only the generic message, but the 3rd attempt already appends '(2 pokušaj(a) preostalo)' because the condition is `remaining <= 2` (remaining=2 at count=3). Use `remaining <= 1` if the counter should only appear from the 4th attempt.

allow_origins=[FRONTEND_URL, "*"] together with allow_credentials=True. Starlette currently echoes the request origin so it works, but the literal "*" entry should be removed - with credentials a wildcard is invalid and this is a security/config smell.

_login_attempts is a plain in-memory dict: cleared on every backend restart, not shared across workers, and never garbage-collected (unbounded growth / DoS memory vector). Also no counter window expiry for non-locked entries ('first_attempt' is stored but unused).

integration_issues.issue: After clicking logout on /beauty-studio-bor/admin, URL becomes /login instead of /beauty-studio-bor/admin/login. handleLogout's navigate() is overridden by ProtectedRoute's <Navigate to="/login"> which fires as soon as AuthContext user turns null.
Same as admin: worker@salon.com logout ends on /login, not /beauty-studio-bor/admin/login.

action_items: Fix ProtectedRoute (and ProtectedSuperAdmin) in /app/frontend/src/App.js to redirect to `/${slug}/admin/login` when a slug param exists, so the tenant-specific login page is used on logout/session loss; keep /login only for super_admin routes. The AdminDashboard.handleLogout change alone cannot work because the router unmounts the dashboard first.
Optionally change the remaining-attempts threshold from `remaining <= 2` to `remaining <= 1` so the counter appears only on the 4th attempt as specified.
Remove the literal "*" from CORS allow_origins while allow_credentials=True.
Consider persisting/limiting the brute-force tracker (TTL cleanup or Mongo/Redis) so it survives restarts and cannot grow unbounded.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js ProtectedRoute hardcodes /login for unauthenticated redirect - this is the actual cause of the wrong logout redirect and also breaks tenant-specific redirect on token expiry.
auth_routes.py leaks 'remaining attempts' info earlier than specified and mixes lockout state in module-level mutable global; not multi-worker safe.

success_rate.frontend: 50% (brute-force UI + role dashboards pass, both logout-redirect cases fail)

rca_of_the_issue: Logout redirect: logout() clears AuthContext user -> ProtectedRoute re-renders with user=null and returns <Navigate to="/login" replace/>, unmounting AdminDashboard; the subsequent navigate(`/${slug}/admin/login`) in handleLogout is discarded (and even if ordered first, the replace navigation to /login wins). Fix must be in ProtectedRoute, using useParams().slug to build the tenant login path.
